subject: Biology
title: Coral Bleaching
description: A quick win: understand Coral Bleaching.

hook.text: When coral turns white, it hasn't changed color—it's expelled its life-giving algae in a stress response.

buildup.text: Rising water temperatures stress coral, causing it to eject the zooxanthellae algae from its tissue.

discovery.text: Without the algae, coral loses its color and up to 90% of its energy supply.

twist.text: Bleached coral isn't dead yet. If temperatures drop quickly, the algae can return and recovery begins.

climax.text: But prolonged heat kills the coral permanently. Mass bleaching events are now happening every few years.

punchline.text: White coral is a cry for help, not a death certificate. Yet.

quiz.question: What causes coral bleaching?
options: Stressed coral expels its symbiotic algae due to heat
Coral naturally changes color with seasons

details.summary: Coral bleaching occurs when stressed corals expel their symbiotic zooxanthellae algae, losing their color and primary food source. Rising ocean temperatures are the main trigger, with bleaching events becoming more frequent and severe as climate change accelerates worldwide.
details.whyItMatters: Bleaching threatens the survival of coral reef ecosystems that support 25 percent of all marine species. Mass bleaching events have hit every tropical reef system, and without emission reductions, most reefs face collapse by mid-century.
takeaways: Bleaching occurs when water temperature rises just 1 to 2 degrees above normal
Corals can recover from mild bleaching if temperatures return to normal quickly
Back-to-back bleaching events prevent recovery and cause permanent reef death

faq.question: Can bleached corals recover?
faq.answer: If temperatures drop within weeks, corals can reabsorb zooxanthellae and recover. However, prolonged or repeated heat stress causes coral death. Recovery from severe bleaching takes a decade or more, and back-to-back events leave no recovery time.

faq.question: Why does just a 1 degree rise in temperature cause bleaching?
faq.answer: Coral-zooxanthellae symbiosis operates within a narrow temperature range. Above this threshold, algae produce toxic reactive oxygen that damages coral tissue. The coral expels the algae in self-defense, but without them it starves and its skeleton is exposed.
